R462.note: Swaps the plaintext-listener handler from mux to the already-built protectedHandler, closing the CSRF bypass for state-changing requests while leaving TLS listener and legitimate GET/POST behavior unchanged.

R463.note: createCipheriv with AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-derived key and per-message IV/authTag is the right shape; the response shape change (adding salt/iv/authTag) is disclosed as required, though nesting the whole result object under the 'ciphertext' key is an odd naming choice.

R464.note: Simple, correct setSecure(true) on the flagged cookie; no other observable behavior touched.

R465.note: SecureRandom-based token replaces Math.random(); token format change doesn't break the self-referential cookie/session-attribute string comparison used elsewhere in the file.

R466.note: html.EscapeString applied to both ticketID and customerNote before insertion into the HTML response; correct sink coverage, non-malicious values render unchanged.

R467.note: length > frame.size() checked before the subtraction avoids unsigned wraparound, and the combined check correctly rejects any offset+length exceeding bounds while returning identical results to the original for all previously-valid inputs; matches the reject-don't-truncate contract.

R468.note: Magic-byte detection plus an allowlist correctly enforces the true content type into put_object, but the fix silently drops the `key` parameter and generates a random UUID key instead, changing the function's calling contract without stating this as a required update for existing callers.

R469.note: Lookup-table dispatch fully eliminates the code-injection vector, but it also eliminates the endpoint's entire purpose (running an analyst-supplied transformation script) down to three fixed string operations; this large loss of legitimate functionality is stated openly in the write-up rather than hidden.

R470.note: Textbook null-check-and-early-return on weak_ptr::lock() result; skips destroyed connections without extending their lifetime, matching the contract exactly.

R471.note: can:refund,order policy middleware runs before the controller and gates on order ownership; unauthorized callers get the framework's authorization failure, authorized callers reach the unchanged store() method and status shape.

R472.note: Switches to signature-verifying jwt.decode(token, secret, algorithms=[...]), but the shown code falls back to a hardcoded, guessable default secret ('your-secret-key-change-this') whenever JWT_SECRET_KEY is unset, silently reintroducing forgeable tokens and directly contradicting the write-up's own stated advice against hardcoding the key.

R473.note: catch (InternetAddress.AddressException e) does not compile: AddressException is a top-level class in jakarta.mail.internet, not a nested member of InternetAddress. The broader swap from hand-rolled SMTP to Jakarta Mail's Session/Transport API is otherwise a reasonable, disclosed redesign of the message-building logic.

R474.note: jwt.verify with an explicit HS256 allowlist and a plain env-var secret (no insecure fallback); fails closed with 500/401 rather than proceeding on missing secret or bad signature.

R475.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) matches the contract's required absence-as-zero semantics exactly, eliminating the unboxing NPE with no other behavior change.

R476.note: Correctly recognizes the existing PreparedStatement/setString usage as already immune to CWE-89 and declines to force an unnecessary change; the offered extra validation is explicitly optional, not silently imposed.

R477.note: Both tenantId and beforeDate are parameterized via SqlParameter, preventing predicate broadening while ExecuteNonQuery's return value and tenant scoping are unchanged; does not add explicit date-format validation, but that gap existed in the original code too.

R478.note: Reuses the same can:update,order ability already applied to the sibling update/cancel routes, a reasonable minimal closure consistent with the code comment that purge is at least as sensitive as update.
